A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HARoPE research work, and their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. All pages were inspected, including v1 Appendix A. v2 has no appendix; its limitations section retains material from v1, while several appendix figures are omitted.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, class-conditional generation, text-to-image generation, and ablation results in Section 4, with additional generated examples in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original results across the same task families, including revised classification experiments, additional compositional evaluations, and new diagnostic and control experiments.

M1.justification: Equations 7–10 change the core query/key adaptation. v1 applies A_h to both queries and keys; v2 applies A_h^T to queries and A_h^-1 to keys. These are different procedures for general nonorthogonal A_h, although SVD parameterization and identity initialization remain. Retained prose still says the same transform is applied to both, leaving the implementation correspondence unresolved.

E1.justification: v2 adds T2I-CompBench evaluation, including explicit 3D-spatial, complex, and non-spatial compositional tests alongside numeracy and 2D relations. ImageNet, MS-COCO, and the 60k BLIP training collection remain; the BLIP30-to-BLIP3o spelling change alone does not establish different data. The dedicated unseen-resolution classification scenario from v1 is removed.

E2.justification: The MS-COCO comparison, labeled MMDiT in v1 and SD3-medium in v2, gains a quantitative RoPE comparator alongside APE and HARoPE. v2 also adds a separately reported parameter-matched RoPE+SVD control in Table 9 and frequency-tuned RoPE comparisons in Table 10. These introduce substantive controls beyond the retained positional-encoding baselines and shared-SVD ablation.

E3.justification: Classification changes from ViT-B trained for 300 epochs at 224 pixels with batch size 256 to DeiT-Base/Large pretrained for 400 epochs at 192 pixels with global batch size 2048, followed by 20 epochs at 224 pixels. v2 also evaluates FLUX at 512 and 2048 pixels in addition to 1024, and introduces a 100k-step DiT frequency sweep. These are reported protocol changes, not evidence of same-setting performance improvements.

E4.justification: v2 adds attention-distance diagnostics across heads and layers, parameter-matched capacity controls, and frequency-base sensitivity experiments. The FLUX head-specialization comparison extends from 500/1000 steps to include 2000/4000 steps. Conversely, v1 Table 6's classification extrapolation analysis and Appendix Figure 9's qualitative head-specialization comparison disappear. Existing matrix-parameterization and DiT resolution ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The new attention-distance visualization summarizes head behavior across images rather than reporting experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Classification results are replaced under different settings: v1 reports 82.76% for HARoPE on ViT-B, while v2 reports 83.76%/84.83% on DeiT-Base/Large. New results include SD3-medium RoPE FID 5.35, compositional scores, and control experiments. At 512 pixels, HARoPE trails RoPE on GenEval (0.758 versus 0.765) and DPG (82.37 versus 82.63); at 2048, GenEval favors HARoPE (0.756 versus 0.735). Main DiT results and 1024-pixel FLUX aggregates are retained, allowing for rounding. Classification extrapolation results and appendix qualitative examples are removed.

T1.justification: The central attention-kernel definition and derivation change from A_h^T R_delta A_h to A_h R_delta A_h^-1. Consequently, the zero-offset kernel changes from A_h^T A_h to the identity, a substantive mathematical difference. Additionally, v2 Equation 9 uses unprimed positions for both queries and keys, which is inconsistent with the displacement-dependent expression in Equation 10.

C1.justification: v2's abstract and methodology overview remove rigid frequency allocation and dynamic frequency reallocation from the enumerated problems and contributions, emphasizing semantic alignment and head specialization. This narrowing is incomplete because related frequency/capacity claims remain in the introduction and conclusion. The central drop-in improvement and relative-position-preservation claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations attributing gains to semantic alignment rather than added parameters or simple frequency tuning, and interprets high-resolution improvements as mitigating extrapolation issues. It also explains specialization through attention-distance distributions. These interpretations do not address the newly reported 512-pixel regressions. The limitations concerning image-only evaluation and static transformations are unchanged from v1 Appendix A.1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code release statement and URL, identifies the previously generic MMDiT backbone as SD3-medium, describes the new capacity control, and explains attention-distance computation. It also adds parameter/FLOP reporting while dropping the earlier MMDiT testing-FLOP entries. Repository contents and accessibility cannot be established from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for T2I-CompBench++ and the original DeiT training paper, while removing DeiT III and numerous peripheral references, including GQA, BERT, BLIP3-o, and Wan. Section 2's substantive positioning relative to RoPE-ViT, STRING, and Rethinking RoPE remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most introductory, related-work, and concluding prose and the main section progression are retained. Targeted revisions expand the SVD explanation and experimental discussion, remove the frequency-allocation subsection, and move limitations from Appendix A.1 to Section 6. Affiliations and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: The document switches from a single-column layout to two columns, substantially rearranging and resizing figures and tables. v1 Table 3 is split into separate SD3 and FLUX tables, and the head-specialization comparison changes from Figure 5 to Table 7. New SVD and attention-distance figures and control tables are added; appendix image panels are removed. Several existing qualitative panels and heatmaps are retained at different sizes and locations.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the empirical evidence with additional comparators, capacity and frequency controls, compositional evaluations, and code-access information. However, the changed method equations remain unreconciled with the prose, the multidimensional formula contains an inconsistency, and claims of consistent superiority overlook the new 512-pixel regressions. These unresolved specification and interpretation problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the stronger experimental coverage.
